items.title: How do you find meaning of life at 41?
items.summary: Happy Thanksgiving! This question crossed my mind in the morning. It feels like I have seen pretty much everything under the Sun. I have modest house (still renting), small kids, a okayish job. I spent time on daily activities and occassionally on long walks. The progress with AI and impact on Software is frankly exciting and depressing at the same time. What are people my age doing these days? How do you keep yourself excited for the future and not feel anxious? Curious to see from a bit older people here how are you doing and challenging yourself well into 40s, 50s and 60s.

deep.body: Happy Thanksgiving! This question crossed my mind in the morning. It feels like I have seen pretty much everything under the Sun. I have modest house (still renting), small kids, a okayish job. I spent time on daily activities and occassionally on long walks. The progress with AI and impact on Software is frankly exciting and depressing at the same time. What are people my age doing these days? How do you keep yourself excited for the future and not feel anxious? Curious to see from a bit older people here how are you doing and challenging yourself well into 40s, 50s and 60s.

comments.text: “Wendell Berry’s formula for a good life and a good community is simple and pleasingly unoriginal. Slow down. Pay attention. Do good work. Love your neighbors. Love your place. Stay in your place. Settle for less, enjoy it more.” Find joy in the routine, life experience, and moments, and stay curious. If you’re not on stable footing, keep working to get there. If you are, and if interested, help others where you are with what you have.

> What are people my age doing these days? preparing a handoff to the next generation theyll sink if handed a political economy theyll stay afloat with plenty of room to swim if handed a data economy https://github.com/systemaccounting/gradienterp
Creating. Drawing. Painting. Helping others.
If you have to ask, you won't find it.

You can only control what you control. But you can do your best to leave the world a little better than you entered it. You have kids: What can you do to ensure their world is better than yours was? People get hung up on reaching some level of money or career but at the end of the day that isn't what's going to matter or make you feel positive about your life. You're at the halfway mark, you still have a lot of time to make an impact.

Learning new skills - not for work, but for hobbies. Woodworking and turning, furniture making, sewing, needle lace. Still painting and drawing and working in glass, too. And I spend time just taking care of my home and forest, and trying to help my kids grow into their own selves. The future will be what it will be. Maybe tech will takes us to the utopia some people believe in, maybe society will crash and burn down to ashes and we are all subsistence farming to survive. Either way, humanity exists and we live our lives. (Unless AI kills us all or people keep burning fossil fuels and make the planet unlivable.) But I gotta say, as an older person, people who are looking at a sweeping change in tech and thinking that it changes the meaning of life are way too siloed into the tech world. Tech is not the meaning of life. Never was. Go out and see what this world has to offer.
Trying to leave the world better than I found it. Trying to care for myself so I can care for others. Trying to cultivate more kindness, compromise, empathy, cooperation.

I am turning 40 next year, and I am freaking afraid of it. I don't know how I missed my earlier years, I don't remember much of it. I don't have a stable income, a home, or a family, and everything seems scattered. Yesterday morning, out of nowhere, I stumbled upon astrology, and it gave me hope. It basically told me that I had to pass through bad planetary alignments, and now the good ones are coming. I thought for a moment, maybe it is this hope that keeps us alive. I know I cannot change anything drastically in a single day or month, but this type of hope is bringing me back to life. A hope for something beautiful. Today is not exactly what I hoped for in my childhood, but at least my life has been somewhat better than it was back then. All I have been doing is taking one step at a time, and it has been really tough.

deep.body: There have been questions about why the /ask page ( https://news.ycombinator.com/ask ) was running dry of Ask HNs - e.g.: Ask HN: Why is Ask HN only showing me 14 posts? - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49984484 - Oct 2026 (47 comments) Ask HN: Why is pagination gone on "Ask HN", and showing only 19 items? - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50280719 - Oct 2026 (3 comments) I believe I found the problem. The pool of stories for https://news.ycombinator.com/ask has traditionally been drawn from the ranked stories list from which we generate the frontpage. That list is restricted to the top 1500 ranked submissions, and it seems the % of submissions which are text posts (i.e. no linked URL) had declined enough to starve the Ask HN feed. The solution is to compute a separate list of ranked Ask HNs. p.s. "Ask HN" is the conventional name but it means text posts. The title can also start with "Tell HN" or nothing in particular. They're just posts which were submitted without a URL.

comments.text: That’s pretty funny! I’ve seen optimizations like this for reporting systems where rather than taking the top N item matching filter X, they cheat by taking the top M (where M > N) items and then filter it client side to N items matching filter X. As long as the results are enough to populate the page you don’t notice the difference and it’s usually faster as you reuse the prior ranking. But if not, you get this exact situation.

items.title: SimDrop – Running iOS simulators in the macOS Finder sidebar
items.summary: Hi HN, I made a small macOS utility for my own iOS simulator workflow. I kept running into two annoyances: getting config files in and out of a simulator is clunky (digging into CoreSimulator UUID folders or running simctl), and on the iPhone Duo simulator I couldn't even drag and drop images onto the window at all. SimDrop puts every running iOS simulator in Finder's sidebar (under Locations) with two folders: - Downloads/ (Files app > On My iPhone > Downloads) - Photos and Videos/ (the simulator's Photos library) Simulators appear when they boot and disappear when they shut down.

deep.body: Hi HN, I made a small macOS utility for my own iOS simulator workflow. I kept running into two annoyances: getting config files in and out of a simulator is clunky (digging into CoreSimulator UUID folders or running simctl), and on the iPhone Duo simulator I couldn't even drag and drop images onto the window at all. SimDrop puts every running iOS simulator in Finder's sidebar (under Locations) with two folders: - Downloads/ (Files app > On My iPhone > Downloads) - Photos and Videos/ (the simulator's Photos library) Simulators appear when they boot and disappear when they shut down. Everything is also reachable from the terminal under ~/Library/CloudStorage/SimDrop-SimDrop/. A couple of caveats up front: - Dragging moves files by default (same as iCloud Drive, because it uses File Provider on the startup volume)—hold Option to copy. - macOS 15+ and iOS simulators only (not physical devices). It's free, open source (GPL-3.0), signed and notarized, and installable via Homebrew: brew install --cask rxliuli/tap/sim-drop Just sharing in case others run into the same friction—feedback or PRs welcome!
